query: What in an incident's description tends to signal it's a hardware problem?

per_column.name: hw_device_mentions
per_column.rationale: Extracts interpretable hardware device categories (printer, server, monitor, keyboard) from the description that can be grouped and compared against whether the incident is hardware-related. Categories are well-separated and human-meaningful, directly supporting relationship discovery. Multi-value cells are a minor cleanliness issue but do not obscure interpretability.

per_column.name: hw_symptom_signals
per_column.rationale: Captures interpretable symptom categories (not_working, malfunction, failure, physical_symptom, unable_to_boot) derived from description text. These form clear, comparable segments that a human can cross-tabulate against the hardware focus to see which phrasings signal hardware problems.

per_column.name: hw_signal_score
per_column.rationale: An aggregate count (0-5) of hardware signals present. It is an opaque composite that essentially restates/pre-answers the focus rather than opening an external relationship. It bundles the very cues under investigation into a score, so grouping on it is circular and not independently interpretable.

per_column.name: hw_signal_flag
per_column.rationale: A binary derived directly by thresholding the hardware signals; it is essentially a proxy for the focus variable itself. Comparing the focus against a restatement of the focus yields no informative external relationship.

judge.rationale: Two of the four columns (hw_device_mentions, hw_symptom_signals) are genuine, interpretable associational variables with well-separated categories that let a human explore which description cues co-occur with hardware incidents. The remaining two (hw_signal_score, hw_signal_flag) are aggregate/binary restatements of the very signals under study and effectively pre-answer the focus, offering circular rather than informative comparisons. The set supports meaningful exploration but is diluted by the restating columns, and both useful columns share a high NULL rate that limits comparison coverage.
